kyoto_saruuya_demachiyanagi.gf_detail: Not GF: burgers on bakery buns, sandwiches on country bread, curry (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_saruuya_demachiyanagi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef burgers, chicken and bacon-egg sandwiches; herbal teas and lemonade are the plant-based options seen (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_saruuya_demachiyanagi.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–22:00 (last orders food 21:00, drinks 21:30); closing days may vary (Tabelog). No table reservations — only course bookings (2 hours, from ¥3,500) (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 34 seats with counter, sofas, tatami and a loft upstairs; non-smoking inside, smoking area in the garden; the toilet is out in the back yard (Tabelog; May 2026). The front looks like a bicycle shop (November 2025). By Keihan Demachiyanagi Stn exit 2 and a bus stop (Tabelog; January 2026).
kyoto_saruuya_demachiyanagi.notes: [Cafe · Demachiyanagi, burgers in an old house] A dim, homey cafe in a renovated old house by Demachiyanagi Stn — sink into a sofa or the upstairs loft for big burgers on bakery buns, country-bread sandwiches, curry and herbal tea. Easy to miss: the front looks like a bicycle shop. Some found portions generous, one found the dishes small for the price; it can be chilly in winter. Cash only; open till 22:00.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a cafe and burger shop by Demachiyanagi with course bookings for groups. Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe a renovated old house of two floors with a loft, antique decor, assorted sofas and accessories for sale at the entrance.

anecdotes.text: A November 2025 visitor hesitated at the door because the front looks just like a bicycle shop.
An October 2025 lunch guest thought two burgers had arrived, so large was the single burger ordered.
A January 2026 visitor on the way to Shimogamo Shrine found the cafe a little chilly and warmed up with the pumpkin soup.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: カフェ・ハンバーガー、左京区田中下柳町14、京阪出町柳駅2番出口、毎日 11:30〜22:00 (L.O.フード21:00、ドリンク21:30)、定休日は変わることあり、席のみの予約不可 (コースのみ、2時間制、3,500円から)、カード・電子マネー・QR 不可、34席、カウンター・ソファ・座敷、禁煙 (庭に喫煙所)。口コミ (2025年10月〜2026年6月、英語): 古い家を改装、2階はロフト、アンティーク、自転車屋のような外観、大きなハンバーガー、パン屋のようなバンズ、ダブルチーズバーガー、アボカドバーガー、ハンバーガーとドリンクのセット1,500円、田舎パンのサンドイッチ (マスタードチキン、ベーコンエッグチーズ)、かぼちゃのスープ、カレー、ハーブティー、レモネード、トイレは裏庭、量が多いとの声と、値段のわりに少ないとの声、冬は少し寒い。

cultural_comfort.note: Cash only; toilet in the back yard; sofas and a loft.

existence.note: Tabelog listing; reviews through June 2026.

kyoto_panel_cafe_gion.gf_detail: Not GF: souffle pancakes, burgers and chips (2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_panel_cafe_gion.vegan_detail: Not vegan: egg-rich souffle pancakes with soft serve, bacon-and-egg pancakes, burgers (2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_panel_cafe_gion.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–17:30, last order 16:00; irregular closing days (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, but not same-day at weekends and holidays (Tabelog). Waits of 30 minutes to an hour at busy times (2024–2026 reviews). Order and pay at the register before being seated; one food order per person (September 2026). No toilet inside — guests are sent to a public toilet (August and September 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 80 seats inside and on a dog-friendly river terrace; non-smoking; takeaway (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews). In the evenings the space runs as Dining Bar W (Tabelog). 2 min walk from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_panel_cafe_gion.notes: [Pancakes · Gion Shijo, river terrace, dogs welcome] A chic cafe known for wobbly, pudding-soft souffle pancakes topped with brulee and soft serve, plus burgers, with a riverside terrace where dogs are welcome. Order and pay first; expect a queue, and book on weekdays. Several 2026 reviewers note it is popular with overseas visitors; some found the pancakes average or pre-cooked. No toilet inside.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a cafe opened 20 January 2020 near Kawaramachi, known for souffle pancakes and burgers, with a pet-friendly terrace; registered as an official listing. In the evening the space operates as Dining Bar W.

anecdotes.text: A reviewer who returns with a dog chooses it for the riverside terrace, and waited about an hour on a May 2025 visit.
An August 2026 visitor found the pancakes average, seemingly pre-cooked and thin, and was disappointed by the lack of a toilet.
Several 2026 reviewers mention that many of the guests are overseas visitors (August–October 2026).

The ¥1,000 lunch — a daily meat or fish plate such as chicken katsu with tomato sauce, with rice, miso soup and a self-serve coffee — is one of the best deals near the station. At night it turns French-leaning bistro with wine and courses from about ¥5,300. Cash only; closed Sunday.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: owner-chef 折橋正明 trained for 17 years in French cooking at a well-known Kyoto hotel, then opened a bistro-style “French-based yoshoku restaurant” on this plot in front of Kyoto Station, held by the family since the grandfather’s generation; the restaurant marked its 21st anniversary on 15 March 2023. Vegetables come from contract farmers in Yagi, Kyoto.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: “good to look at, delicious to eat, and something you want to eat again” — so that diners of every age can eat favourite dishes to the full.
chef_bio.specialty: Daily lunch plates and homemade curry.

anecdotes.text: A November 2025 couple found a Showa-era yoshoku place in front of the station that had not changed for the tourists.

kyoto_tower_sand_bar.gf_detail: Ask. A beer-led bar (beer contains gluten) with small snacks such as smoked quail eggs and canapés (2026 reviews); no gluten information.
kyoto_tower_sand_bar.vegan_detail: Ask. Drinks plus a few snacks — smoked quail eggs, smoked salmon, mascarpone canapés (2026 reviews); no vegan information.
kyoto_tower_sand_bar.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); open all year (Tabelog). Order at the register or by phone at the table; mobile orders take only cards, PayPay or Rakuten Pay (May and July 2026). Cards (JCB) and QR incl. PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). A U-shaped counter of 12 seats plus standing room for 14, with food-hall tables around it; food from other stalls can be brought in (Tabelog; April and August 2026). Non-smoking; smoking area outside (Tabelog). B1F of the Kyoto Tower Building, straight in from the underground passage from Kyoto Stn (Tabelog; October 2026). Opened 14 April 2017 (Tabelog).
kyoto_tower_sand_bar.notes: [Bar · Kyoto Tower basement, craft beer by the station] A U-shaped bar in the food hall under Kyoto Tower, reached straight from the station underpass: Kyoto craft beer, Sorachi and Sapporo on tap with a choice of pour, Kyoto sake and whisky, and smoked snacks — or bring food from the other stalls. Open daily 11:00–23:00; a handy wait for the Shinkansen.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a bar, café and standing bar in the B1F food hall of Kyoto Tower Sando, opened in April 2017, with sake and wine. Kyoto Tower Sando itself is run by 京阪流通システムズ (2021 press release); no operator is given for the bar.

anecdotes.text: An April 2026 office worker stops in after work for a SORACHI 1984 schooner and liked the seasonal flowers on the counter.
An August 2026 visitor enjoyed a Kyoto whisky but found the glass still wet from washing.
An October 2026 traveller with 30 minutes before a train had a sharp-pour Black Label and found more seating than expected.

kyoto_salman_sohel_halal.gf_detail: Ask. Biryani, rice sets, kebabs and curries alongside naan (2025–26 reviews); naan contains wheat; no gluten information.
kyoto_salman_sohel_halal.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options; lunch sets include a vegetable curry and lassi (November 2025, June 2026); no vegan information.
kyoto_salman_sohel_halal.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00 (last order 22:30), closed irregularly (Tabelog; official site). Reservations accepted; party plans; take-away and delivery (Tabelog; official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and e-money (Tabelog). 42 seats incl. a private room for 10–12 per Tabelog (the official site says 62). Non-smoking; wheelchair access; free Wi-Fi; children welcome with a kids' menu (Tabelog). English menu (Tabelog). Northeast corner of the Kojinguchi crossing, 1 min from the Kojinguchi bus stop, 7 min from Jingu-Marutamachi (Keihan) (official site; Tabelog). The English site says the Islamic Culture Center mosque is a 2-minute walk.
kyoto_salman_sohel_halal.notes: [Halal Indian, Arab and Turkish · Kojinguchi, by the Kamo river] A bright, roomy halal restaurant by the Kojinguchi crossing whose own site states "ALL HALAL FOODS": fragrant dum biryani, curry lunch sets with naan, lamb and chicken kebabs, hummus and Afghan-style rice. Wine is also served (Tabelog). Open daily to 23:00; English menu; take-away and delivery.

chef_bio.chef_name: アリ セック シラジ
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the chef opened the restaurant to serve authentic Indian, Persian and Arab food in Kyoto, cooked with carefully chosen ingredients that meet halal standards; the site was published in December 2020. A November 2025 review mentions a chef trained in hotel restaurants.
chef_bio.philosophy: Halal food is a Muslim food-safety standard that anyone can eat with confidence (official site greeting).
chef_bio.specialty: Dum biryani; Indian, Arab and Turkish dishes.

anecdotes.text: An April 2026 regular on an eighth visit tried a new Afghan rice dish and ordered the Kashmiri naan by mistake, which came with pomegranate and coconut.
A February 2026 diner was surprised how quickly the mutton biryani arrived, with attentive service.
A June 2026 visitor found the mutton vindaloo closer to a mutton butter chicken and the meat a little tough.

kyoto_masaru_yoshida.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a fried-food yoshoku diner — cutlets, fries, kara-age, demi-glace (2023–25 reviews).
kyoto_masaru_yoshida.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat and fish set meals with miso soup (2023–25 reviews).
kyoto_masaru_yoshida.hours_raw: Hours not listed on Tabelog; reviews describe lunch visits (2023–25). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). 15 seats: four tables for 4, one for 2 and a counter of 5 (Tabelog; August 2023). Non-smoking (Tabelog). In the residential streets east of the Kamo river, across from the Kyoto University pharmacy campus, about 5 min from the Konoe-dori bus stop (June 2023, December 2024).
kyoto_masaru_yoshida.notes: [Yoshoku diner · Yoshida, by the Kyoto University hospital] A family-run neighbourhood diner across from the university pharmacy campus, feeding locals, medical students and doctors: the signature melt-tender pork-belly toro katsu, hamburg steak with demi-glace and big fried-food sets from about ¥1,000. Cash only; hours not published — go at lunch.

roles: Grandmother of the family, front of house
chef_bio.background: A June 2024 review describes a family business: the chef is the son of the family, and the grandmother — who has eight grandchildren — works in the shop. An August 2023 review saw several generations in the kitchen.

anecdotes.text: A June 2024 family stopping between appointments at the nearby immigration office found the whole family who run it wonderfully kind to the visiting couple’s four-month-old son.
A May 2024 diner caught the limited pork-belly toro katsu at noon on a weekday and praised its thin batter.
A December 2025 diner could not finish the Set A of beef cutlet and three kinds of fry.
